candidate: Confirmation rule with harness-drawn fresh seeds (pattern from lora-speedrun JUDGING.md, commit 1436658, 2026-08-04)
what: Before a change is kept, the harness (not the agent) draws new seeds after the working tree is frozen, reruns, requires every rerun to clear the bar, records the mean and never the best, allows one confirmation per tree hash, and treats gaps inside the measured spread as ties.
problem_here: Goal 1 and quality attribute 1: a kept result must not depend on a lucky seed or on re-rolling until it passes. The kit records seeds but nothing stops seed or rerun shopping.
mechanism: expctl draws seeds from OS entropy at confirm time, stores them with the tree hash, refuses a second confirm for the same hash, and compares the mean with baseline plus noise floor.
evidence: https://github.com/Saivineeth147/lora-speedrun/blob/main/JUDGING.md read 2026-11-11. Rule written and applied by the project maintainer to 6 records; one record passed by 0.09 points on one of three runs. No controlled study of the rule itself.
maturity: Spec frozen 2026-07-18; last commit 2026-08-04; MIT; 151 stars and one maintainer (weak adoption signal).
cost: Stdlib code in expctl. Extra training runs per kept change. Failure mode: real gains smaller than the spread are discarded.
simpler_alternative: A fixed seed list in the config (cheaper, but the agent can tune to it).
reason: Implements 'harness code decides what is kept' with no dependency; its cost is compute that the user-set budget already bounds.
cheap_local_trial: On a 2-minute toy training script: confirm with 3 drawn seeds, then try to confirm the same tree again and check the refusal. CPU is enough.

candidate: Clean-process evaluation with a pinned-hash manifest (pattern from lora-speedrun SECURITY.md, commit 1436658)
what: Evaluation starts in a new process and clean environment, re-hashes evaluator code, evaluation data and base weights against a committed manifest, and aborts on any mismatch.
problem_here: The frozen evaluator is protected by a path guard on agent tool calls. A training script the agent wrote can still alter caches, installed packages or data files that the evaluator reads later.
mechanism: Extend expctl hash to a manifest check that runs first in every confirmation and final evaluation; run the evaluator in a fresh interpreter, not in the training process.
evidence: https://github.com/Saivineeth147/lora-speedrun/blob/main/SECURITY.md read 2026-11-11: separate eval sandbox built from a clean image, pins re-hashed first, threat table names cache poisoning and sitecustomize tricks. Design argument by the maintainer; no incident data.
cost: Hashing multi-GB weights takes seconds to minutes per evaluation. Without a container a poisoned interpreter environment is still not excluded.
simpler_alternative: Keep the path guard only.
reason: Closes the gap between 'the agent cannot edit the evaluator' and 'the evaluator ran on what was pinned'; stdlib hashing only.
cheap_local_trial: Change one byte of a pinned evaluation file between training and evaluation; the evaluation must abort. Minutes, no GPU.

candidate: Repository noise floor from unchanged-baseline repeats (A/A runs) as a precondition of keep-or-revert
what: Run the unchanged baseline several times, with new seeds and at least twice with the same seed, store the spread per evaluator hash, and keep a change only if its gain exceeds that spread.
problem_here: Quality attribute 2 asks for gains 'by more than run-to-run noise'; the kit has an uncertainty reference but no measured floor that code enforces.
mechanism: expctl baseline with a repeat count writes mean and standard deviation; the keep rule reads them.
evidence: arXiv 2608.03887 v1 (2026-08-04, single author, per-seed data published): an identical configuration with the same seed and hardware gave SD 0.104 in a retention ratio. arXiv 2609.22257 v1: 0.256 vs 0.415 on one condition across runs. lora-speedrun JUDGING.md: gaps below spread are ties. All read 2026-11-11 (papers at abstract or HTML level).
maturity: Standard statistical practice; sources are 2026 preprints and one project protocol.
cost: Extra baseline runs per evaluator version; long runs make the repeat count small and the estimate rough.
simpler_alternative: A user-set minimum gain.
reason: Without it the loop keeps noise; the same-seed result shows that fixing the seed does not remove the need.
cheap_local_trial: Run the repository's baseline 3 times with one seed and 3 times with drawn seeds on the 32 GB GPU; compare the two standard deviations.

candidate: Hypothesis-count control: untouched confirmation split or family-wise correction for the unattended loop
what: Count how many hypotheses were scored against the validation split, show the count beside every kept result, and confirm the final result on data the loop never scored against.
problem_here: Quality attribute 1 scenario (50 experiments overnight): selecting the best of many on one split inflates the kept score even with an honest evaluator.
mechanism: expctl counts scored experiments per evaluator and split hash; an optional confirmation split is scored only by the confirm command; the sealed test set stays single-use.
evidence: arXiv 2605.15394 v1 (2026-05-14): 22 auxiliaries, best +2.53 points at p = 0.003 uncorrected, none survives Holm-Bonferroni, 5-seed replication null. arXiv 2503.13507 v1 (2025-03-13): top entries of a fine-tuning competition overfit open benchmarks. Abstract level, read 2026-11-11.
maturity: Textbook statistics; evidence from one audit paper and one competition report.
cost: A third split costs data; small datasets may not afford it; correction lowers power.
simpler_alternative: Report only the count of hypotheses tried.
reason: A frozen evaluator stops cheating, not selection bias; this is the missing half of validity for a many-run loop.
cheap_local_trial: Pure-Python simulation: 50 null experiments drawn from the measured noise SD; count false keeps with and without the confirmation split. Seconds.

candidate: Standard-library preflight audit of dataset, config and metrics log (check list drawn from gradian 0.1.0 diagnostics)
what: A command that reads the training data file, the config and, after a run, the metrics log, and reports silent fine-tuning faults before GPU time is spent.
problem_here: The guard checks agent tool calls; nothing checks the training setup itself (train-eval duplicates, empty or truncated targets, no supervised tokens, unset seed, no eval set, schedule not finished).
mechanism: Hash-based duplicate and train-eval overlap checks, empty and prompt-equals-target checks, conflicting answers, length outliers, seed and eval-set presence, then NaN, plateau, spike, always-clipping and unfinished-schedule checks on the log. Tokenizer checks (loss-mask coverage, EOS, chat template) only when the user's stack is importable.
evidence: https://gradian.dev/docs/diagnostics (v0.1.0, 2026-08-10) lists 41 checks without thresholds; nobody has measured how often each fires or what it saves. PEFT v0.21.0 notes (#3534) confirm one such silent fault in a major library. Read 2026-11-11.
maturity: Idea; the source catalogue is a one-commit alpha (Apache-2.0).
cost: A few hundred lines. False positives teach the agent to ignore it. Thresholds need dated defaults.
simpler_alternative: A written checklist in the fine-tuning reference.
reason: The faults are documented and cheap to detect, but the benefit is unmeasured; build a small subset and measure on planted faults before making it default.
cheap_local_trial: Plant 5 faults in a toy JSONL dataset and log (rows shared by train and eval, empty targets, missing seed, truncated completions, NaN) and check each is reported. Minutes, CPU.

candidate: Trainable-parameter and adapter-target assertion at run start
what: Record the number of trainable parameters when a run starts and fail if it is zero or differs from the plan; for adapters, fail if the target pattern matched no module.
problem_here: A run that trains nothing, or the wrong layers, still produces a loss curve and a score; neither the guard nor the run states catch it.
mechanism: runlog helper that accepts any object with parameters() (no framework import), writes the count to the run record; expctl compares it with the config.
evidence: PEFT v0.21.0 release notes (2026-09-15), PR #3534: add_adapter aimed at non-existent layers used to adapt nothing without a message and now raises. lora-speedrun TASK.md counts every saved tensor against a cap. Read 2026-11-11.
maturity: Fix shipped in PEFT 0.21.0; the helper is an idea.
cost: About 20 lines; none at run time.
simpler_alternative: Require PEFT 0.21.0 or later (covers PEFT only).
reason: One integer per run removes a class of invalid results.
cheap_local_trial: Add a second LoRA adapter with a misspelled target module on a small model; the helper must flag an unchanged parameter count. Minutes.

candidate: Versioned evaluator with a known-answer self-test
what: The evaluator carries a version and a small fixture of outputs with expected scores; the fixture runs before each confirmation and final evaluation, the version is stored with every result, and a version change forces a new baseline.
problem_here: Freezing the evaluator protects against edits, not against a wrong metric; a later fix silently makes old and new results incomparable.
mechanism: expctl selftest gains an evaluator fixture step; results are keyed by evaluator hash.
evidence: PEFT v0.20.0 release notes (2026-07-28): maintainers found a bug in the forgetting metric of their own benchmark and republished numbers. arXiv 2611.10658 v1 (2026-11-07): a customary metric (0.977) hid a model that loses to a mean baseline (0.076 vs 0.267). Read 2026-11-11.
cost: The user writes 5 to 10 fixture cases once.
simpler_alternative: Hash freeze only.
reason: A maintained public benchmark shipped a wrong metric; a ten-case fixture is cheap insurance.
cheap_local_trial: Put an off-by-one into a toy exact-match scorer; the self-test must fail. Minutes.

candidate: Provenance fields on every result row, including a dirty-tree flag
what: Each result stores tree hash, dirty-tree flag, evaluator hash, data manifest hash, environment lock hash, hardware fingerprint, all seeds and package versions.
problem_here: Partly covered by expctl hash, env and snapshots; to check: dirty flag, hardware fingerprint and environment hash on each result row, so a reviewer can verify a kept result from saved artifacts.
mechanism: Fields added to the run record that expctl already writes.
evidence: lora-speedrun JUDGING.md: reports carry hardware fingerprint, harness commit, env.lock hash and seeds. PEFT v0.21.0 PR #3385 adds a git dirty flag to benchmark results; its suite stores package versions with commit hashes. Read 2026-11-11.
maturity: Both sources are in use in 2026.
cost: Small; repositories without git need a file-hash fallback.
simpler_alternative: Current snapshot only.
reason: Two independent projects converged on the same fields.
cheap_local_trial: Compare the fields that expctl env and expctl hash print today with this list. Minutes.

candidate: Baseline rows (untuned model, trivial predictor, frozen prompt) and a task-metric-decides rule
what: Every comparison includes the untuned model and a trivial predictor scored by the frozen evaluator with a frozen prompt; the configured task metric decides and loss is logged but never decides.
problem_here: A loop can keep a change that lowers loss but not the task score, or report a tuned model that is below the untuned one.
mechanism: expctl baseline stores the two rows per evaluator hash; the keep rule refuses candidates below the untuned row.
evidence: arXiv 2611.12628 v1 (2026-11-09; 3 models, 3 seeds): bits-per-byte separates models in every seed while chrF++ does not (30.51 vs 30.61); the ranking of gains depends on the zero-shot prompt. arXiv 2609.22257 v1: automated fine-tuning fell below the untuned model on 2 of 9 tasks. arXiv 2611.10658 v1: a mean baseline beats a published model. Abstract level, read 2026-11-11.
cost: One extra evaluation per evaluator version; the user must define the trivial predictor.
simpler_alternative: A line in the journal template.
reason: Cheap, and it turns two documented failure modes into visible table rows.
cheap_local_trial: Score the untuned base model and a majority-answer or copy-input predictor on the validation set. Minutes on the GPU.

candidate: Structured experience records in the journal (pattern from SAGE, arXiv 2609.22257 v1, 2026-09-06)
what: Journal entries become records: strategy (method, data, format, hyperparameters), change vs baseline and vs parent run, conditions under which the finding held, verdict (useful, useless, harmful) and date, retrievable by later sessions and by the scouting step.
problem_here: Goals 1 and 2: a long loop without memory repeats failed ideas; the journal is free text.
mechanism: One JSON line per experiment beside the markdown journal; retrieval by task type and method; verdicts updated when a finding is re-tested.
evidence: Authors' own measurement on 9 unseen tasks with 1.5B models: average relative improvement 3.2% without stored experience, 15.6% with it (mean of 3 runs). No code, no replication. Insights applied outside their category fell below baseline on one set. https://arxiv.org/html/2609.22257v1 read 2026-11-11.
cost: Template and index in stdlib. Risks: findings reused outside their conditions, and a file that grows beyond what the agent should read.
simpler_alternative: Keep free text and add one machine-readable header line per entry.
reason: The only measured lever for automated fine-tuning in this sweep, but single-source; try the header-line form first.
cheap_local_trial: Convert 10 existing journal entries to records and check whether a fresh agent session retrieves the relevant one for a new hypothesis. Minutes, no GPU.

candidate: Measured memory probe step before long runs
what: Launch the planned command for a few steps at the planned batch size and longest sequence, record peak GPU memory, compare with the card and store planned vs measured.
problem_here: An out-of-memory crash an hour into an unattended run wastes budget; expctl has no memory planning.
mechanism: expctl launch with a probe option; peak read by polling nvidia-smi through subprocess or from a field the training script reports through runlog.
evidence: The best-documented formula estimator (canifinetune 0.4.0, own prospective validation, 4 cases) is off by 29 to 64%, so a formula cannot decide: https://daoyuanli2816.github.io/can-i-finetune-this/validation-0.4.0/ read 2026-11-11. No measurement of the probe itself.
cost: About a minute per launch; polling misses short peaks; needs longest-batch-first ordering to see the true peak.
simpler_alternative: Let the run crash and rely on the existing stall and failure states.
reason: Cheap and stdlib, but unproven; measure how well a 3-step peak predicts the full-run peak.
cheap_local_trial: Under WSL2 on the 32 GB GPU: probe a QLoRA config for 3 steps, then run 200 steps and compare peaks. About 10 minutes.

candidate: Quarantine of agent-instruction files inside third-party code
what: Instruction files in cloned, vendored or installed third-party trees (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude, .agents, agent-docs, llms.txt) are treated as data: never auto-loaded, never copied by the installer, and third-party repositories are read by the scouting step only as summaries.
problem_here: The brief forbids acting on fetched instructions; cloning a training framework puts the same kind of text on the agent's default reading path.
mechanism: A rule in the default instructions, a guard warning when the agent opens such a file outside the repository's own root, and a documented per-agent setting for nested instruction files.
evidence: Seen on 2026-11-11 in repositories from this sweep: oumi (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md), miles (AGENTS.md, .agents, .claude), halo (agent-docs, AGENTS.md), Soup (AGENTS.md), gradian (llms.txt plus a README passage addressed to agents). No incident measured.
cost: False warnings in monorepos that nest their own instruction files; auto-load behaviour differs per agent and must be tested.
simpler_alternative: One sentence in the default instructions.
reason: Extends an existing must-not to a path the brief does not name; the rule costs one sentence, the guard check should be tried per agent.
cheap_local_trial: Put a nested AGENTS.md with a harmless marker instruction in a subfolder and see on each supported agent whether it is loaded. Minutes.

candidate: Out-of-domain guard metric (retention or side-effect probe) reported beside the task metric
what: A second fixed probe set outside the task domain, scored before and after fine-tuning; a kept change must not lower it by more than the noise floor.
problem_here: Fine-tuning can damage prior skills or shift unrelated behaviour while the task metric improves; the kit has one configured metric.
mechanism: Optional second metric entry in the kit config with its own frozen evaluator command.
evidence: arXiv 2608.03887 v1: plain LoRA fine-tuning kept 62.9% of HumanEval pass@1, 84.1% with a penalty (10 seeds, single author). arXiv 2611.12864 v1 (2026-11-09): in- and out-of-domain behaviour shifts are linked across hyperparameters. https://github.com/leo-dcfa/ai-latent-bias-transfer: 18 runs, shifts of d 0.9 to 2.2 that perplexity did not show (one individual, unreplicated). Read 2026-11-11.
cost: The user supplies the probe set and scorer; one more evaluation per run; a judge-model scorer would add a network dependency.
simpler_alternative: A journal field stating whether side effects were checked.
reason: Relevant mainly to language-model fine-tuning; evidence is recent and thin, so offer it off by default.
cheap_local_trial: LoRA-tune a 0.5 to 1.5B model for about 7 minutes on the 32 GB GPU and score 50 unrelated prompts before and after.

candidate: Remote artefact sync and stop-before-cap in the rented-GPU module
what: Copy checkpoints and logs off the rented machine on a schedule and stop the job before the spend cap or account balance is reached.
problem_here: Goal 3 and quality attribute 3: no lost work and no runaway spend; provider behaviour at zero balance can be deletion.
mechanism: Periodic pull by the local controller, plus a cap check that uses elapsed time times price.
evidence: https://passo.uno/fine-tuning-docs-llm/ (2026-06-05): two adapters lost when pods were deleted at zero balance (one first-person account, Unverified). DeepWiki index of oumi-ai/oumi (Inferred): the launcher has no budget cap and auto-stop is unavailable on providers that cannot stop instances. Read 2026-11-11.
maturity: Idea; provider documentation not checked by this scout.
cost: Credentials for the provider or storage (attack surface); transfer time and egress cost.
simpler_alternative: Manual download at the end of the run.
reason: Fits a hard constraint of the brief, but the supporting evidence is an anecdote; confirm from provider documentation first.
cheap_local_trial: Dry run against a second local directory standing in for the remote; a real test needs a rented machine and money.

candidate: Coverage or entropy as a second signal, and a checkpoint pool, for RL-style and staged post-training
what: Log coverage over k samples or output entropy beside the primary metric and keep more than the best-validation checkpoint when a checkpoint feeds a later stage.
problem_here: The kit selects by one metric; for staged post-training the best-scoring checkpoint can be the worst starting point.
mechanism: Extra metric fields in runlog; retention policy keeps several checkpoints.
evidence: arXiv 2610.01509 v1 (2026-10-01): post-trained models often lose to base models on pass@K in 42 cases (no numbers in abstract). ICML 2026 workshop poster https://icml.cc/virtual/2026/82731: peak pass@10 0.806 to 0.481 with deeper SFT, 3 seeds. arXiv 2611.12799 v1: up to +7.4 points from discarded checkpoints. All authors' own; read 2026-11-11.
maturity: Preprints and a workshop poster from 2026.
cost: k-sample evaluation multiplies evaluation cost; more checkpoints use disk.
simpler_alternative: A paragraph in an optional RL reference.
reason: Applies to RL-style runs, which are not the common case in the brief; evidence is small-n.
cheap_local_trial: Compare pass@1 and pass@8 of a base and a fine-tuned 1.5B model on 100 short problems. Under an hour on one GPU.

candidate: lora-speedrun task (spec frozen 2026-07-18, commit 1436658) as a benchmark for the kit itself
what: A frozen fine-tuning task (Qwen2.5-1.5B on GSM8K, at least 57.0% exact match, adapter-only, wall-clock score) with a public record history; the same agent runs it with and without the kit under one budget.
problem_here: Brief preference: a cheap, rerunnable measure of whether the kit helps; quality attribute 2.
mechanism: Local command for one run on a 24 GB+ card; runs take 22 seconds to 12 minutes plus evaluation; record history gives known targets.
evidence: README, TASK.md and JUDGING.md read 2026-11-11; 6 records verified by the maintainer with 3 fresh seeds each. Forum criticism (overfitting to one task, 2 to 5% timing jitter) is user-generated; the overfitting risk is corroborated by arXiv 2503.13507.
maturity: Created 2026-07; last commit 2026-08-04; MIT; 151 stars; one maintainer; official timing needs a paid cloud account.
cost: PyTorch stack, model download, GPU. Timings on another card are not comparable with the board. The pass gate reuses the public test split. An agent with network access can copy public records.
simpler_alternative: A tiny CPU task defined inside the kit's own selftest.
reason: Closest thing found to a minutes-long, externally defined fine-tuning task with a referee protocol; its weaknesses are known and documented.
cheap_local_trial: Under WSL2 on the 32 GB GPU: one baseline run (about 12 minutes of training plus evaluation) after the user approves fetching the repository and model.

candidate: PEFT v0.21.2 method-comparison suite and results Space as the dated evidence source for adapter variants
what: Maintainer-run comparison of adapter methods on one task (MetaMathQA to GSM8K) with accuracy, forgetting, memory, time, file size and pinned versions; experiments are append-only.
problem_here: Brief must-not: undated technique advice. The fine-tuning reference should not name adapter winners from memory.
mechanism: The scouting step and the hypothesis menu cite the Space with the date read.
evidence: https://github.com/huggingface/peft/tree/main/method_comparison and release notes v0.20.0 to v0.21.2, read 2026-11-11. Measured by the library maintainers on their own hardware; one task, one base model family; the suite's forgetting metric had a bug fixed in v0.20.0.
maturity: Library first released 2023; v0.21.2 on 2026-10-01; Apache-2.0; widely used.
cost: Needs network to read. One benchmark only. Results near 0% or 100% are not comparable.
simpler_alternative: none found (papers compare on their own setups)
reason: Best same-hardware evidence found for the most common fine-tuning choice; costs one link and a date.
cheap_local_trial: none needed to read it; reproducing one row takes a few hours on high-end consumer hardware by the suite's own rule.

candidate: canifinetune 0.4.1
what: Formula-based preflight estimate of fine-tuning memory and a starting recipe, without PyTorch and without downloading weights.
problem_here: Out-of-memory failures waste launches; the kit has no memory planning.
mechanism: Adds up weights, quantisation, gradients, optimizer state, activations, logits and overhead from model metadata.
evidence: The project's own prospective validation of v0.4.0 (4 predeclared cases, one RTX 4080 on native Windows): mean absolute error 46.2%, all overestimates, 0 of 4 false-feasible, and no accuracy gain over 0.3.0. https://daoyuanli2816.github.io/can-i-finetune-this/validation-0.4.0/ read 2026-11-11.
maturity: First release 0.1.1 on 2026-06-10; 0.4.1 on 2026-10-04; MIT; 795 stars (weak signal); WSL GPU not qualified.
cost: A pip package needing Python 3.10+; conservative estimates may reject feasible configs.
simpler_alternative: The measured probe step.
reason: Honest validation, but 46% error cannot gate a launch; useful at most for choosing a starting config.
cheap_local_trial: Estimate one QLoRA config, then compare with a measured 3-step probe on the 32 GB GPU. Minutes (needs a package install the user approves).
